summary: The Gambia admits ECOWAS citizens, the UK, Canada, Australia and much of northern Europe without a visa — the UK government says British visitors are stamped in for 28 days, which can be extended twice by 28 days — while citizens of much of the Caribbean, the Pacific, East and Southern Africa and South-East Asia need an entry clearance that their host in The Gambia has approved by the Immigration Department, and US, French and various other passport holders need a visa.

AF.notes: Afghanistan is on the Immigration Department’s list of countries whose citizens need both a visa and an entry clearance. The department says visas are issued by Gambian embassies, missions and consulates abroad and by immigration officers at the gazetted entry points; your host in The Gambia must also obtain the entry clearance from the Immigration Department.

source.name: Gambia Immigration Department — visa services (visa exemption and visa lists)

BF.notes: Burkina Faso left ECOWAS on 29 January 2025, but the ECOWAS Commission has announced that its citizens continue to enjoy, until further notice, movement, residence and establishment without a visa under the Community’s protocols; The Gambia’s Immigration Department says citizens of Mauritania, Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso “will enjoy privileges as accorded”. The Commission also recognises, until further notice, their national identity cards and passports bearing the ECOWAS logo. The ECOWAS Commission says the 90-day stay limit for Community citizens was repealed by Supplementary Act A/SA.1/07/14 but has yet to be implemented; no official source we could read states the stay The Gambia applies.

source.name: ECOWAS Commission — Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger's withdrawal from ECOWAS is now a reality

payments.text: Australia's Smartraveller says The Gambia is a cash-based economy: many hotels, restaurants and shops don't accept credit cards (major hotels generally do), and few ATMs accept foreign cards. The UK FCDO adds that there are not many ATMs outside the Senegambia tourist area, and Canada says US dollars, euros and CFA francs are widely accepted.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says petty theft is a problem in cities and tourist areas, especially at night on isolated beaches, in markets and at crowded events, that young men known as 'bumsters' approach tourists on the beaches, and that security checkpoints are common on all major routes.

tips.text: The UK government says British visitors are stamped in for 28 days and can get 2 extensions of 28 days from the Immigration Office in Banjul or the tourist police stations in the Tourism Development Area. Ireland says Irish citizens may stay up to 90 days.

Australia's Smartraveller says malaria occurs year-round across the country, and the Government of Canada recommends antimalarial medication for most travellers. Use insect repellent and make sure your accommodation is insect-proof.

The UK FCDO warns of young men known as 'bumsters' who approach tourists, especially on beaches, offering help or guiding and sometimes asking for money. Canada advises politely declining any unsolicited offer.
The UK FCDO warns that 'bumsters' offering tours into Senegal are unlikely to follow the correct immigration procedures, which could get you detained by the immigration authorities.
Bring enough cash for your stay: Australia's Smartraveller says The Gambia is a cash-based economy, many places don't accept credit cards and few ATMs accept foreign cards.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for The Gambia?
faq.answer: Citizens of ECOWAS states and of much of northern and western Europe — including the UK, Ireland, Germany, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, Sweden and Finland — enter visa-free, as do Canadians and Australians; the UK government says British visitors are stamped in for 28 days, and Ireland says Irish citizens may stay up to 90 days. Citizens of much of the Caribbean, the Pacific, East and Southern Africa and South-East Asia need no visa but an entry clearance, which their host in The Gambia has approved by the Immigration Department. US, French, Portuguese and various other passport holders need a visa, which the Immigration Department says is issued by Gambian embassies, missions and consulates abroad and by immigration officers at the gazetted entry points.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for The Gambia?
faq.answer: Yes. The Immigration Department lists the United States among the countries whose citizens need only a visa (no entry clearance). It says visas are issued by Gambian embassies, missions and consulates abroad and by immigration officers at the gazetted entry points.

faq.question: How long can I stay in The Gambia?
faq.answer: The UK government says British visitors are stamped in for 28 days on arrival and can get 2 extensions of 28 days from the Immigration Office in Banjul or the tourist police stations in the Tourism Development Area, and Ireland says Irish citizens can stay up to 90 days. The Immigration Department says a short visit visa is issued for a period of 90 days.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccine for The Gambia?
faq.answer: WHO lists The Gambia as requiring a yellow fever certificate from travellers aged 9 months and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, a list that includes neighbouring Senegal. Australia's travel advice goes further and says you need a valid yellow fever certificate to enter The Gambia.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit The Gambia?
faq.answer: No official source names a best time to visit. The UK FCDO and the Government of Canada say the rainy season runs from June to October, when flooding can disrupt roads; November to April falls outside it.
